passage: Gurleen waited until the tractor noise faded from the lane and then sat on the charpai beside her son Nilesh. "Beta, your father and I will not live in the same house any more," she said. Nilesh's chin trembled. "It is nothing you did. We both love you, and that will not change." She said nothing against his father, though the words sat in her throat. Tomorrow he would still go to school, and on Sunday they would still make parathas. When Nilesh whispered, "Can I ask you things later?" she said yes. She did not ask him to carry a message to his father or to keep her secrets.

qa.q: Where did Gurleen sit when she told Nilesh about the separation?
qa.a: She sat on the charpai beside him.

qa.q: Why did Gurleen say nothing against Nilesh's father even though the words sat in her throat?
qa.a: She wanted Nilesh to feel secure and not caught in the middle, so she kept her own hurt to herself.

qa.q: What routines did Gurleen point to in order to steady Nilesh?
qa.a: She reminded him he would still go to school and that on Sunday they would still make parathas.

qa.q: How might Nilesh have felt as his mother spoke?
qa.a: His chin trembled, so he was probably sad and frightened, and her calm words and promises about routines may have given him some steadiness.

grounding: A parent explains the split calmly, says it is not the child's fault, keeps routines and avoids using him as a messenger.
